title: How GitGuardian Secures the Credential Layer: From Discovery to Remediation
content_md: TL;DR: Credentials stay valid long after exposure : Exposed secrets are a standing risk because 64% of secrets confirmed valid in 2022 were still valid in January 2026, and they travel across repos, pipelines, laptops, and tickets. Context turns detection into decisions : Secret Analyzers show what a credential can access, and the Exploration Map shows its consumers and resources, so teams know who owns it and what breaks if it is revoked. One platform covers detect, remediate, prevent : Monitoring spans repos, CI/CD, public GitHub, and developer endpoints, with workflows, vault onboarding, and validity rechecks to confirm the old credential no longer works. Modern enterprises run on credentials; those pieces of data that enable all of our services, infrastructure, AI, and fellow humans to connect together and get their work done. This takes many shapes; for example, API keys connect applications to services. Access tokens allow automation to interact with infrastructure. Service accounts keep production systems running. AI agents use credentials hardcoded in MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers to access the tools and resources they need to complete their tasks. Every one of those secrets represents real access. When a credential is exposed, an attacker may gain the same access as the person, application, or machine it belongs to.
